newsitem.title: POLAND: INTERVIEW - Budimex eyes domestic expansion.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Budimex eyes domestic expansion.

text.p: Polish construction firm Budimex SA plans to shift the focus of its activities from exports to the domestic market where it sees better growth prospects, the firm's president said on Thursday.

Grzegorz Tuderek told Reuters in an interview he saw Budimex's share of the overall Polish construction market rising to three percent in the next few years from the present 1.2-1.4 percent. The share of domestic sales in Budimex's total revenues was seen rising to about 50 percent in 1997 from last year's 20 percent due to the shift in focus.

He said the Polish residential construction market, now in a deep slump as the two-digit inflation keeps financing prohibitively expensive, should offer the biggest growth prospects once the market started to recover.

"What we mostly count on is residential construction... we have a potential to build 3,000 or 4,000 apartments every year, now we build only 1,000...but we believe the situation will change," Tuderek said.

He said that in two or three years' time residential construction should stage a dramatic recovery as interest rates were expected to fall in line with declining inflation, putting mortgage loans within reach of average Poles.
Tuderek said that within 2-3 years residential construction could account for 10-15 percent of the Budimex group's sales, from less than five percent now.
Budimex's group sales were seen rising to 640 million zlotys in 1997, from last year's estimated 445 million.

Tuderek said Budimex, which has 46.3 percent in a consortium bidding for Poland's highway scheme Austrostrady SA, saw the project as another lucrative domestic possibility, with 100 kilometres of a highway costing about $330 million.
"We will try to focus on...rest areas, so our participation might be significant as infrastrucure costs amount to about 15 percent of the whole highway construction costs," he said.
Tuderek said the planned takeover of Budimex Trading SA could temporarily dilute earnings per share due to a new share issue for Trading's stockholders.
But in the longer term Budimex's shareholders should benefit from the company gaining market share.
"I believe it's a good deal...any time we can sell Budimex Trading's assets, hotels, we also have the possibility of taking mortgage loans," he said.
In the take-over Budimex will issue two million new registered, preferred shares for Trading shareholders in two-for-one share exchange.
The new shares will be excluded from public trade for two years so Budimex shares price should not suffer from increased supply following the deal, Tuderek said.
Tuderek also said Budimex was likely to benefit from Kredyt Bank, current Budimex Trading 56-percent owner, boosting its 15-percent stake in Budimex after the merger.
"We would be very glad if Kredyt Bank had a stake of about 30 percent of votes...the cooperation we had so far is perfect," he said.
Tuderek said Budimex and Kredyt Bank had been doing business together in the former Soviet Union countries with Kredyt Bank supplying financial services for Budimex contracts.
